title: rustman.report/v1
description: A Rustman report: a run (kind: run), an exploration (kind: exploration), a contract check (kind: contract) or a load test (kind: bench). Every text field is redacted: secret values appear as «redacted:<name>».

interrupted.description: Stopped by Ctrl+C; the requests are partial.

jsonrpc.description: The JSON-RPC side of a kind: jsonrpc request: the envelopes sent and received per call, every HTTP attempt, and a subscription's events (the first 1000). Absent from every other request. Added in v0.5.

id.description: The id sent; null for a notification.

response.description: The envelope that answered this call, or null.

grpc.description: The gRPC side of a kind: grpc request (protocol grpc): the call type and transport, the final status with decoded details, response headers and trailers (binary values in base64), every received message, the message timeline of streaming calls and timings; or, when the call ended without a status, the error and its kind (config or request). Absent from every other request. Added in v0.5.

realtime.description: The realtime side of a kind: ws or kind: sse request: the handshake, the message timeline (at most max_timeline entries, payloads above 64 KiB cut to a preview), how many entries were dropped and how the session ended. Absent from every other request. Added in v0.6.

body.description: The body of a refused upgrade (at most 64 KiB).

size.description: The full payload size in bytes.

type.description: text, binary, json, ping, pong, close, a system note (connect, reconnect, error) or the SSE event type; at most 1 KiB.

payload.description: Text, or binary data in base64; at most 64 KiB.

truncated.description: The payload was cut to 64 KiB, or the type or id to 1 KiB.

id.description: The SSE event id; at most 1 KiB.

data_row.description: The data row a data-driven (--data) run used; absent from every run without --data (--iterations included). Added in v0.2.

server_timings.description: The response's Server-Timing metrics, in order; absent when it has none. Added in v0.6.

snapshot_counts.description: How the run's snapshot assertions ended; absent when the run had none.

snapshot_result.description: The outcome of a `snapshot` assertion. Every value is redacted.

path.description: The snapshot file, relative to the workspace, with `/`.

snapshot_diff.description: The differences from the stored snapshot.

text.description: The unified diff of text bodies.

path.description: A JSONPath into the body, or `status` or `headers.<name>`.

trace.description: The trace context the request carried (trace propagation on, or a traceparent/B3 header the request set). Absent otherwise. Added in v0.6.

backend_trace_id.description: The trace id of the response's traceresponse, when it differs from trace_id; links use it.

start_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the exchange started.

end_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the exchange ended.

link.description: The trace link, when a link template is configured (redacted).

Settings.description:
Everything a resume repeats: the probe selection, the seed, the safety
flags and the budgets.

Family.description: A probe family (`--probes`), in plan order.

Severity.description: How bad a finding is, most severe first.

finding.description: Probes that produced at least one finding.

failed.description:
Probes whose request failed or whose chain stopped early, without a
finding.

SeverityCounts.description: A count of findings per severity.

operations.description: Operations that answered at least once.

Ratio.description: A part of a whole, with its percentage (one decimal).

StatusCell.description: One documented status of one operation.

oneOf.description: Nothing was sent for the operation: the safety policy refused it.

Cell.description: The state of one documented status in the coverage matrix.

remediation.description: How to fix it, from the rule registry.

probes.description: The probes it occurred in, in plan order.

ReportFinding.description: One finding, de-duplicated per rule and operation.

body.description: The start of the response body (at most 4 KiB).

truncated.description: The body was longer than the excerpt.

trace.description: The trace context the request carried; absent without one.

Evidence.description: The redacted exchange behind a finding.

backend_trace_id.description: The response's `traceresponse` trace id, when it differs.

EvidenceTrace.description: The trace ids of an evidence exchange (trace-propagation spec).

curl.description: The evidence request as a curl command; secrets are `{{name}}`.

request.description:
A request file (YAML) sending the evidence request to `{{baseUrl}}`
and asserting what a correct API answers.

ProbeResult.description: One probe and how it ended.

path.description: Its path relative to the target, as a template (`/users/42`).

url.description: Its URL, redacted, as reports show it.

delete.description: `METHOD /path` of the documented operation that deletes it.

Resource.description: A resource a probe created, identified by a captured id.

Cleanup.description: One deletion of a created resource, after the probes ran.

tags.description: Its tags, in document order; the first groups it in JUnit.

OperationInfo.description: One documented operation: how reports group and locate it.

producer.description: `METHOD /path` of the operation whose response provides the value.

consumer.description: `METHOD /path` of the operation that uses it.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer into the producer's response body, e.g. `/id`.

Dependency.description: A value one operation's response provides to another's parameter.

spec.description: The OpenAPI document, as a resume finds it.

settings.description: The probe selection, safety flags and budgets.

left_behind.description: Created resources that were not deleted, oldest first.

cleanup.description: Deletions of created resources, in the order they ran.

operations.description: The documented operations, in document order.

dependencies.description:
Data dependencies between operations: a value from one operation's
response used as a parameter of another (the API graph of the viz
companion). Added in 0.1; absent in older reports.

oneOf.description: `rustman contract diff`: differences between two OpenAPI documents.

`rustman contract pact verify`: Pact interactions replayed against a
provider.

`rustman contract verify`: recorded exchanges checked against a
document.

ContractMode.description: Which contract command wrote the report.

role.description: What it is to the command: `old`, `new`, `spec`, `pact`, `history`.

ContractSource.description: One document or file a contract command read.

counts.description:
Items per status, in the mode's order (for a diff: breaking,
non-breaking, unknown), including statuses with no item.

passed.description: `true` when no item fails the command.

ContractSummary.description: The counts of a contract report.

StatusCount.description: How many items have one status.

allowed.description: The allowlist entry's justification, when one accepted the item.

failing.description: Whether the item fails the command.

locations.description:
Where the item is, the primary location first (for a diff, the new
document).

ContractLocation.description: A place in one of the report's sources.

observed.description: Documented operations with at least one exchange.

operations.description: Every documented operation, in document order.

ContractCoverage.description:
Which documented operations recorded traffic exercised (passive
conformance).

violations.description: Exchanges of this operation with a violation.

OperationCoverage.description: One documented operation and the exchanges that matched it.

sources.description: The documents and files checked, such as a diff's `old` and `new`.

catalog_version.description: The rule catalog version a diff classified with.

items.description: In the command's order (for a diff, the document order).

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems, such as expired or unused allowlist entries.

coverage.description:
For a conformance check: the documented operations the recorded
traffic exercised.

BenchProfile.description: The load profile, as the flags gave it.

Aborted.description: Why a bench stopped before its end.

iterations.description: Iterations that ran to their end.

iteration_duration.description:
How long those iterations took, from their first request's start to
their last one's end (think time excluded).

scheduled.description: Iterations the open model scheduled (0 for closed models).

dropped.description: Scheduled iterations that found no free VU.

rps.description: Requests per second over the whole run.

generator_lag_p99_ms.description:
The 99th percentile of the load generator's scheduling lag: how
late its timers fired. Above 10 ms the results may be
generator-bound.

BenchTotals.description: The counts of a whole bench.

oneOf.description: Closed models: the time each request took.

The open model: measured from the scheduled start (coordinated
omission corrected).

LatencyKind.description: Whether latencies include queuing before the iteration started.

LatencySummary.description:
Latency percentiles in milliseconds, from an HDR histogram with 3
significant digits; all 0 without requests.

phases.description: Average time of each phase, over the requests that had it.

bytes_sent.description: Approximate: the request line, headers and text body as recorded.

StatsSummary.description: The statistics of one request file, or of every file together.

PhaseSummary.description:
Average phase timings in milliseconds; a phase no request went
through (no new connection, no TLS) is absent.

file.description: The request file, relative to the workspace root, with `/`.

phases.description: Average time of each phase, over the requests that had it.

bytes_sent.description: Approximate: the request line, headers and text body as recorded.

FileSummary.description: The statistics of one request file.

second.description: 1 for the first second of the run.

active_vus.description: VUs running at the end of the second.

actual.description:
The measured value, such as `412ms` or `0.20%`; `n/a` when there
was nothing to measure (`checks` without assertions).

at_ms.description: Milliseconds since the start of the run.

target.description: The `--target` origin: the only one requests could go to.

aborted.description: Why the bench stopped early; absent when it ran to its end.

files.description: One entry per request file, in collection order.

series.description: One point per second of the run.

thresholds.description: Every threshold, in the order given.

error_samples.description: At most 20 per error class, in the order they happened (redacted).

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems, such as a generator-bound run.
